6) month as it seems they've given up on me. I have developed a lot of pain in the neck and upper back over recent years, that is undiagnosed.

3) After a while I got through to my GP that the stomach issues hadn't abated despite excluding gluten. Got sent for lactose intolerance test: positive.I was now convinced that with the stomach/bowel issues addressed a period of recovery and then an exercise regime would result

2) ME was diagnosed in my mid 20s in a labyrinthine way. I complained of pain and muscle spasms and stomach/bowel issues.They diagnosed me with depression.Around five years later they took me seriously on the stomach issues.I was eventually diagnosed non coeliac gluten intolerant

Nobody really knows for sure (it's nascent science), but one theory is that the autoimmune system is going through extreme trauma and is overeacting.I carried on even though I was fatigued and experiencing manageable pain (joints, muscles), breathlessness .Big mistake

4) Of course, the 7 years it took to explain the bowel/stomach issues didn't explain many of the other symptoms; so another five year fight to diagnose CFS/ME was the next stage. A diagnostic journey that started in 2005 and ended in a diagnosis in 2017. The most difficult thing?
